items.note: Story 1: LVCCA organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president, creamery 1891.
Story 1: paid on pounds of butterfat by test not weight; test of the station of delivery governs.
Story 1: 'under payment by weight, a faulty test would have cost nobody a dollar.'
Only Wilbur Teague appears in Section A; Effie Loomis and Hobart Sill are never named.
Son of Gideon is stated, but the run gives manager from 1911 (planted error), not 1913.
Story 6: yearly 'station gain ... five and a quarter per cent, as usual' line, more fat received than credited, carried to the general account.
Story 1: Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Core mechanism present: milk weighed and sampled, fat read on a bottle neck ruled for a fixed charge, cream to Larrow Green, skim returned. 'Composite' is not stated.
Story 2: Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Story 2: full invoice, 6 doz pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., total $77.93.
Stories 3-4: deficit flat at 0.19 in every month, June flush and February alike.
Nothing says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette and that the county had none.
Keddie 1861-1934, 29 seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Test book kept in his own hand from 1896 (the bolded element).
Summary-leaf figures 3.80 (1896) and 3.61 (from 1898) appear nowhere in Section A; 3.61/3.80 are given only in C and G.
Story 5: nine weeks, 8 May to 10 July 1911, borrowed measure, tests higher then back, question mark. The run says the size of the rise is unknown, so 3.80 is missing, but the core fact is present.
Story 3: Emmet was Orra Keddie's brother; the tester's wife's brother was the biggest loser.
The 1919 circular is present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why) is missing; both required.
Died February 1934; book impounded 1925, went to the Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897; the scales agreed.
Story 4: first complaint on record 1902. The Hollow-vs-Green gap is never given as 0.19.
The committee came in January and reported in March 1908, but the run never states that the sampling covered Jan-Feb-Mar 1908. Nyle Grigg is only implied via 'Grigg's sleigh'.
Story 3: 1910, 200,000 lb on 3.42; proportional error (every reading 5% low; true 3.60).
Passed to Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, to Hazel 1962.
Cudd factory at Alder Corners, Vessey County, but Redlow Ridge is never named ('over the ridge' only); the key gates on the ridge.
Four of the six farms hauled over the ridge in the summer flush. 1915 is not stated; core fact present.
Independence: tested by another house in another county (Vessey), and the Alder Corners figures as artifact.
Ostrey Hollow read 0.19 lower than the same milk elsewhere, flat in every month, wet years and dry.
Same milk tested by another house read differently; used to defeat the hay theory.
Rosalie is Jerome's daughter (niece rejected); she had the figures copied for Ivy in 1958.
Strawn is named and 'related to nobody', but his visits are dated from 1908 (NT-23 planted error); 1907-1936 is not given.
Lactometer at every visit, never found added water.
12 June 1923, against a calibrated burette, condemned the whole lot.
Only 'drew no inference' (context). Nothing says he wrote no figure for the deficiency or made no report beyond the condemnation.
The 1924 average is given as 3.85 (planted error); the key requires 3.80.
Crate to the loft over the intake room; notebooks to the state office in 1936 and the Farland library in 1947.
Petition January 1925.
Board 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two in the weigh room. The chairman is 'an Ashlin attorney', not named Frick; core fact present.
Section A never presents watering, theft and bog hay as the three explanations argued before the board with none accepted.
Four books named, including Strawn's 1923 notebook; nobody laid it beside the test book.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 ahead of a finding of 'no cause'; 4 May 1925, $3,800 without admission, charged to the station account.
One fifth of $19,000 is stated, but the award is never tied to the account where the loss had built up as 'gain' since 1898.
Ivy b.1931, granddaughter, State Agricultural College at Farland, Leland Vaught.
Her sources are listed, but the point that these records had never been in the same room is not made in Section A (it appears only in G).
February 1958, crate in the loft, nine surviving.
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 vs 17.6, 95% of mark; 0.88 short stated in Story 2.
'Every fat reading 5% low' is stated, but '3.61 recorded where 3.80 stood' is absent from Section A.
40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb and $19,000 are present, but the identity of 76,000 lb with the summed station-gain entries is not stated in A (only implied in C3). All four are required.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; 24 years after death, 33 after dismissal, 35 after the crate went up.
Granddaughter.
Duncan's daughter; Duncan is Ansel's son.
Second cousins, derived via Roy and Duncan being first cousins.
Leaves full vs half siblings open (pre-1889 diary pages lost) and says the degree holds either way.
Gideon Vose, father.
Gideon's Article VII made the test decisive; his son blamed the patrons rather than question it.
Headline verdict 'no relationship'. This is an assertion.
Resolves by family testimony instead of saying no document settles it and that a family denial is not a record.
$90.00 via 360 x $0.25, stating explicitly that it uses the long-run average price because no 1910 price is in its sources; accepted under the key's exception.
76,000 lb; 5.26% of credited and 5.00% of received, denominators named.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
26 years 1 month 11 days; 25 full years 1898-1922, part years explained.
Abstention A02: cannot be determined.
Variable: the measuring glass, borrowed in place of the station's own.
Tester, herds, pasture/hay, scale, acid, patrons held constant.
Result given only as 'rose markedly' and 'dropped back'; 3.80 and 3.61 are not stated.
Cause follows the glass, not the man or the feed; theft and hay fail. Limits: size of error, whether every pipette was short.
1911 interval (r22/r24/r18), ledger surplus (r23), Alder Corners (r17/r18), 1923 switch (r22).
Independence argued; ledger and 1911 hold without the 1958 measurement.
Abstention A09 answered 'No.' This is an assertion.
Yes, he knew the tests ran low: 1919 circular, complaints from 1902.
Only two of the five valid elements (signed the ledger sheets, 1919 circular). Manager date given as 1911; no hearing argument; no 'never names glass'.
Abstention A03 not declined: the verdict sentence 'What the sources show he did not grasp was the meaning of the ledger line' asserts he did not know.
Found, resolved and method given: weigh book 1900 vs 1897; Orra 1868 vs 1866; Keddie start '95 vs 1896; 1908 committee vs 1925 board. Capped at 3.
NT-14 ($77.39, r19+r20, broken by summing the invoice) and NT-18 (great-niece, r19+r22, broken by r18 and Falke's correction). No other pair identified as a pair.
A04 (accident vs substitution, works books burned 1931). A06 not addressed. A10 abstained only in Section A, poles not identified, not in E.
r20's 'nothing before 1900' vs the 1897 invoice; r18's 1868 vs 'eighty-two in 1948'.
Pipettes 16.72 vs 17.6, 95%, 3.80 to 3.61, proportional; onset 1 May 1897 and end 12 June 1923 with nothing on the farms changing. Its 1924 3.85 is deducted separately.
Watering (Vose) defeated by the lactometer, the agreeing scales and the ledger surplus.
Theft defeated by the station gain (theft makes cream light), the 1911 interval, and the post-1923 rise under the same tester.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214 (0.05 winter, nothing summer) against a flat 0.19.
Abstention A07 answered 'No.' This is an assertion.
Abstention A05 answered 'That the cause was in the glass.' This is an assertion.
Counted at exactly 150 words.
Invoice, ledger, weigh book, inspector's notebook, rival's test book (plus the 1958 measurement).
Decoys presented only as blame; no wrong headline figure.
